method: Per-business live check: fetch the listed website (HTTPS validity, CMS/builder and staleness signals, booking capability), then search dated public sources for trading evidence (review dates, Companies House filings, food-hygiene ratings, council and tourism listings). records.name: Groves Chemist
records.tradingEvidence: Local first-hand report 24 July 2026 confirms trading. Corroborated by dated public listings: the National Pharmacy Network and BestCareCompare both carry Groves Chemists Ltd at 165–167 Main Street, Dundrum, BT33 0LY (028 4375 1326), and an active Facebook page exists. A family-owned business with a second branch, Killough Pharmacy (028 4484 2915).
records.digitalPresence: Dead site — and the strongest case in the batch. Liveness probe 24 July 2026 (scripts run locally, DNS resolve4 plus HTTP and HTTPS on apex and www, redirects unfollowed): groveschemist.com resolves (193.200.99.10) and returns HTTPS 200, but the page served is a deactivation notice: "This website is no longer available, If you are the pharmacy owner, please contact The Pharmacy Centre to re-activate." The archived structure behind it shows what was switched off: repeat prescription ordering with user accounts and health records, an online shop of 8,000+ items, both branches with hours, prescription collection from five surgeries and free delivery across BT30 and BT33, plus Pharmacy First, blood-pressure monitoring, contraception and smoking-cessation services. Footer © 2021. Built on The Pharmacy Centre / Medicine Chest platforms.
records.designTask: Restore the capability that was switched off: repeat-prescription request, both branches with hours, the delivery and collection map, and the services list — without the account system that made the old platform expensive to keep.
records.caveats: RECLASSIFIED. Batch two selected this as the round's only first-website case on the basis that no site was found. That was wrong: a full pharmacy site with prescription ordering existed and has been deactivated, leaving a live URL that tells patients nothing. Same-name check: Groves Chemists trades in Dundrum and Killough only — do not conflate with unrelated Groves pharmacies elsewhere.
records.notes: Concept built 24 July 2026, published 26 July 2026, RETIRED 27 July 2026 by the project owner. The deactivation notice on the pharmacy's domain is a centralised platform's — The Pharmacy Centre / Medicine Chest — and what was switched off was that product, not something Groves built. The design task, "restore the capability that was switched off", presumed the pharmacy wants it back; the evidence establishes only that it stopped, and not whether they opted out, let it lapse, or had it retired for them. Proposing to rebuild a platform a business has come off is proposing work they have already declined. Concept page, styles and media removed; see research/concepts/groves-chemist/triage.json.
records.retired: 2026-07-27 — concept retired; rebuilding the centralised prescription platform the pharmacy came off presumes a decision that is theirs to make.

records.name: Tonn Ruray Café
records.tradingEvidence: Live Webflow site with current apartment pricing (£129–£149 per night), an active Instagram (@tonnruray), Facebook and TripAdvisor presence, and a published phone and address (61 Main Street, Dundrum, BT33 0AE; 028 4379 8214).
records.digitalPresence: Live, well-made Webflow site — but built for the apartments, not the café. The homepage leads with 'Sea View Luxury Apartments' and nightly rates; the restaurant appears below it. Navigation is EAT · EXPLORE · CONTACT US · BOOK NOW with Rooms, Restaurant, Spa, Experiences, Offers and About Us beneath. There is no booking engine of any kind: 'Check Availability' and 'Book Your Stay' both resolve to /contact-us, so every enquiry is manual. The café's menu is a PDF stamped JUN24 — two years old at time of verification — and gallery images are dated June 2024. CONTRADICTED 27 July 2026: the homepage capture taken for this concept on 24 July 2026 opens on the café shopfront photograph under the TONN RURAY wordmark, navigation EAT · EXPLORE · CONTACT US · BOOK NOW · Tel, followed by a Gertrude Stein quote on coffee and 'Fresh local ingredients with a seasonal menu' over the café's own food photography. No apartments or nightly rates appear anywhere in the captured scroll. Treat the apartment-first reading above as unverified — either the site changed between 20 and 24 July or the reading was wrong when it was recorded. The JUN24 menu PDF and the manual 'Book Now' handoff are not affected by this correction.
records.designTask: Answers the open question from the selection record — the café is the failing half. Give it its own front door with a live menu that replaces the two-year-old PDF, service times, and a table enquiry, without disturbing the apartment side that the current site serves well.
records.caveats: The apartment side of this site is genuinely good and must be treated as such — the critique is about what the café inherited, not about the build. Two businesses on one domain: be explicit about which one the concept addresses.
records.notes: Concept built 24 July 2026, published 26 July 2026, RETIRED 27 July 2026 by the project owner. The concept was worse than the site it proposed to replace and all four publication checks passed it. The site is a new business's own personal work — its own shopfront and food photography, a chosen Gertrude Stein quote on coffee, a hand-drawn squiggle under See the Menu, one consistent dusty-pink and italic-serif identity — and the concept replaced that with studio typography on cream, seven struck-through dead links and a remark about the owners' room pricing. Its real gap is maintenance, not design: a JUN24 menu PDF two years stale and a BOOK NOW that resolves to a contact form. The published case study also claimed the homepage opened on Sea View Luxury Apartments and nightly rates; our own 24 July capture shows it opening on the café shopfront with EAT first in the navigation, so that claim is unsupported by the evidence we hold. Concept page, styles and media removed; see research/concepts/tonn-ruray/triage.json.

records.name: Newcastle Family Dental Care
records.tradingEvidence: Confirmed trading under its own name, resolving the open question from the selection record. The destination page is branded 'Newcastle Family Dental Care' throughout and lists three named dentists — Dr David Knowles (BDS QUB 2014), Dr Rebecca McCarey (BDS QUB 2014) and Dr Daniel Sandford (Grado en Odontología UCV 2023) — at Iveagh Court, 2 Railway Street, Newcastle, BT33 0SP, open Monday to Friday 9.00–17.00, phone 028 4372 3776. Confirmed trading first-hand 24 July 2026.
records.digitalPresence: Dead site, in the way that matters most for a health practice. Liveness probe 24 July 2026 (scripts run locally, DNS resolve4 plus HTTP and HTTPS on apex and www, redirects unfollowed): newcastlefamilydentalcare.com resolves and 301s — over plain HTTP, not HTTPS — to http://www.djmaguiredentists.co.uk/location-newcastle.html, while www.newcastlefamilydentalcare.com is ENOTFOUND. The .co.uk the practice publishes in its own email address behaves worse: it resolves, but HTTPS times out on both apex and www, and HTTP 301s to the same insecure parent-group page. So a patient who types either domain, or who mails the address on the practice's own stationery, is handed over plain HTTP to a page on another practice's site. The practice's own branding, staff and hours exist — they are just hosted under someone else's roof and served without encryption.

records.name: Hugh McCanns
records.tradingEvidence: Maintained into 2026 despite an out-of-date footer. The menu PDF is served from a 2026/07 upload path — this month — while the footer still reads '© Hugh McCann's 2018'. Published contact 028 4372 6622, info@hughmccanns.com, 119–121 Central Promenade, Newcastle, BT33 0EU, with active Facebook, Instagram and TripAdvisor.
records.digitalPresence: Live and actively maintained, built by Amigo Studios. Three generations of family ownership in a 200-year-old building; weddings for 40–250 guests 'at the foot of the Mournes'; a front bar and restaurant; Little Haven accommodation; and a sister property, the Avoca Hotel. The copy is genuinely good — 'From Today Until Your Day, We Do', 'Passed down through three generations… traditional rustic charm as well as the new world contemporary style'. The gap is capability, not appearance: for a venue whose entire business is booked dates, there is no enquiry form, no availability check and no date capture anywhere on the site. Every wedding enquiry has to become a phone call. Supporting staleness: testimonials run 2017–2019 and the downloadable brochure is '2021.22'.
records.designTask: Feature upgrade, not a rebuild: a date-and-guest-count wedding enquiry that captures the two facts every venue conversation starts with, plus a refreshed testimonial and brochure surface — leaving the site's voice and photography intact.
records.caveats: MAINTAINED SITE — the Buck's Head rule applies in full. The © 2018 footer is weak evidence and must not be used as the argument; the July 2026 menu upload proves active maintenance. The honest pitch is the missing enquiry capability. Highest-value single target in the batch, so the accuracy bar is highest here.
records.notes: Three census records are one business: 'Hugh McCanns' and "Hugh McCann's Cafe/Bar" both scored ~80 as site-less, while the live site was recorded against 'Little Haven Guest House'. That third record is why the false-high was caught at all. All three need merging in the alias table before batch three. Concept page built 24 July 2026 at /concepts/hugh-mccanns/ with its own scoped identity (src/styles/concept-hugh-mccanns.css). Withdrawn during the 27 July fifth-check review because it removed the venue's photography and criticised the current enquiry route inside the proposed page. Repaired the same day with a disclosed faithful dining-room visualisation, customer-facing criticism removed and the mailto handoff corrected to the published info@ address; all five checks and the desktop/390 px route audit pass. Outreach has not begun.
